paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between co-occurrence number and accuracy (ACC %) for different knowledge editing methods applied to a Large Language Model (LLM). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^0 to 10^3 with tick labels at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” using a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 65 with tick labels at 0, 40, 50, 55, and 60, and 65.  There are six lines shown on the plot. The “Base” line is black with circular markers, and it begins at approximately (10^0, 41%) and ends at approximately (10^3, 44%), exhibiting a slight upward trend. The “MEND” line is brown with diamond-shaped markers, starting at approximately (10^0, 44%) and reaching approximately (10^3, 56%), showing a general increasing trend.  The “FT” line is blue with triangular markers, beginning at approximately (10^0, 43%) and ending near (10^3, 48%), with an increasing but less steep trend. The "IKE" line is red with cross-shaped markers, starting at approximately (10^0, 43%) and increasing to approximately (10^3, 52%). The "MEMIT" line is green with square markers, starting at approximately (10^0, 50%) and increasing to approximately (10^3, 55%). Finally, the "ROME" line is green with circular markers, starting at approximately (10^0, 51%) and reaching approximately (10^3, 66%), with a steady upward trend.
